Let me analyze this OIML certificate.

Certificate number: R49/2006-FR2-08.05, revision 2, issued 30 January 2013.
Issuing authority: Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais (LNE), France.
Person responsible: Thomas LOMMATZSCH, Responsable du Pôle certification (Measuring Instruments Division Manager).
Address: 1, rue Gaston Boissier - 75724 Paris Cedex 15. Tél: 01 40 43 37 00, Fax: 01 40 43 37 37, E-mail: info@lne.fr, Internet: www.lne.fr.

Applicant: CONTAZARA, Carretera Castellon Km 5,5, 50720 ZARAGOZA, SPAIN.
Manufacturer: CONTAZARA, Carretera Castellon - Km 5,5, ESP 50720 ZARAGOZA (Spain).

Certified type: Electronic water meter CONTAZARA type CZ-SJ (also written CZSJ in the annex) intended for metering of cold potable water.

Type designations: CZ-SJ, CZSJ; DN 50, 65, 80, 100 variants.

Recommendation: R49, edition 2006.

Accuracy class: 2.

Model family: 4 models: DN 50, DN 65, DN 80, DN 100.

Test reports: "OIML R 49 EVALUATION REPORT N090064-D1-1 (4 pages)" → id: N090064-D1-1, pages: 4, role: type_evaluation_report (evaluation report).

Characteristics table:
- Totalisateur (Indicating device): Electronique (Electronic) → type_level: indicating_device_type: "Electronic"
- DN (mm): 50, 65, 80, 100 → model_level by model DN50, DN65, DN80, DN100
- Q3 (m³/h): 25, 40, 63, 100
- Q4 (m³/h): 31.250 (= 31.25), 50, 78.750 (= 78.75), 125
- Q3/Q1: 250 (all models) → type_level
- Q2/Q1: 1.6 → type_level
- Position: horizontal → type_level
- Length (mm): 300, 300, 350, 350
- Connections: Flanges → type_level
- Maximum admissible pressure (bar): 16 → type_level
- Temperature class: T30 → type_level
- Indicating range (m³): 99 999 999 → type_level
- Verification scale interval (1×10⁻⁵ m³): 20, 50, 50, 100
- Accuracy class: 2 → type_level
- Environmental class: C → type_level
- Electromagnetic influence class: E1 → type_level
- Reverse flow measurement: No (with footnote *) → type_level with footnote marker
- Power supply: Battery / limits: 3.67 V; 3.3 V / lifetime 12 years → type_level: power_supply_type: "Battery", battery_supply_voltage_limits... Hmm, "3,67 V ; 3,3 V" — these are limits of DC supply. Could be min 3.3, max 3.67 V. I'll record power_supply: "Battery", battery_voltage_limits: {min: 3.3, max: 3.67, unit "V"}, battery_lifetime: 12 years.
- Software version: P03v21 → type_level

Footnote: "* The water meter is not designed to measure reverse flow but can withstand an accidental reverse flow without any deterioration or change in metrological properties."

Matrix table: preserve the full table in matrix_tables.

Page total: certificate says annex consists of 1 page(s), and page 2/2 — total document 2 pages. The annex is 1 page. The schema field page_total under certificate — the certificate document says "comprend 1 page(s)" for the annex. The document itself is Page 2/2. I'll set page_total: 2.

Member state: France.

Date issued: 2013-01-30.

oiml_issuer_id: not present explicitly. Omit.

Scheme: A (single-stage, typical OIML-CS). It doesn't say scheme B, so default A.

project_number: "N090064" maybe? The evaluation report is N090064-D1-1. Reference LNE-14195 rév. n° 2. Hmm, project number — I could use N090064 as project. Actually the reference LNE-14195 is the certificate reference. I'll leave project_number omitted or use "N090064". The schema says project_number under certificate. Not clearly present. I'll omit it, or maybe include "N090064". I think safer to omit since not explicitly labeled. Actually "Référence LNE-14195 rév. n° 2" is the LNE reference. I could put it in certificate as project_number? Hmm. It's a document reference, not necessarily project number. I'll omit to avoid fabrication. Actually, maybe include reference in revision_history: revision "2", date 2013-01-30, changes: "Revision 2 of certificate". Revision history: revision "2" (string), date 2013-01-30, changes — "Référence LNE-14195 rév. n° 2" — the changes field: not specified what changed. I'll put "Second revision of certificate R49/2006-FR2-08.05" — hmm that's fabrication-ish. Maybe changes: null or "Revision 2". I'll put revision: "2", date: "2013-01-30", changes: null? Schema requires changes field but rule 8 says omit if not present. I'll include revision_history with changes null... better to omit changes or set it to something neutral. I'll include {"revision": "2", "date": "2013-01-30", "changes": null}.

Models: model_id "DN50", "DN65", "DN80", "DN100". label maybe "DN 50" etc.

model_level characteristics:
- nominal_diameter_dn: values per model, unit mm
- permanent_flow_rate_q3: m³/h
- overload_flow_rate_q4: m³/h
- length: mm
- verification_scale_interval: unit "1×10⁻⁵ m³" — hmm. The unit column says (1X10^-5 m³). So value 20 means 20 × 10⁻⁵ m³. unit_symbol: "×10⁻⁵ m³"? Avoid LaTeX. Use "1e-5 m³" or "10⁻⁵ m³". Unicode superscript is fine: "10⁻⁵ m³". I'll use unit_symbol: "×10⁻⁵ m³" — that's a scaled unit. Alternatively convert: 20×10⁻⁵ = 0.0002 m³ = 0.2 L... but don't convert; keep as given. unit_symbol: "10⁻⁵ m³". I'll leave unit_id null.

type_level:
- indicating_device: "Electronic"
- q3_over_q1_ratio: 250 (dimensionless)
- q2_over_q1_ratio: 1.6
- installation_position: "horizontal"
- connections: "Flanges"
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 16 bar
- temperature_class: "T30"
- indicating_range: 99999999 m³
- accuracy_class: "2"
- environmental_class: "C"
- electromagnetic_influence_class: "E1"
- reverse_flow_measurement: false / "No" with footnote_markers ["*"]
- power_supply: "Battery"
- battery_supply_voltage_limits: {min 3.3, max 3.67} V — the text: "3,67 V ; 3,3 V" — listed as max; min order. So min 3.3 max 3.67.
- battery_lifetime: 12 years (unit "years", symbol "years" or "a"). Use unit_symbol "years".
- software_version: "P03v21"

Accuracy classes: ["2"] — R49 classes are numeric 1, 2. accuracy_classes: [2]? Schema says accuracy_classes[] — could be strings or numbers. Use ["2"].

Category: "Water meter" — the category list in schema examples doesn't list water meter but includes "Gas meter". Use "Water meter".

module_designation: not applicable — water meter. Omit or null. I'll set null? Rule: don't fabricate; the field allows null. I'll omit.

description: "Electronic water meter CONTAZARA type CZ-SJ intended for the metering of cold potable water."

Issuing authority address_lines: ["1, rue Gaston Boissier", "75724 Paris Cedex 15"]. Phone: "01 40 43 37 00" → "+33 1 40 43 37 00"? Keep as given: "01 40 43 37 00". Email: info@lne.fr. Website: www.lne.fr.

Applicant address: ["Carretera Castellon Km 5,5", "50720 ZARAGOZA", "SPAIN"]. Manufacturer: ["Carretera Castellon - Km 5,5", "50720 ZARAGOZA", "ESP"].

Test reports: id "N090064-D1-1", pages 4, role "type_evaluation_report". Date not given — omit.

Certificate number: "R49/2006-FR2-08.05". Recommendation: id "R49", edition 2006 (the 2006 edition — R49/2006). Scheme "A".

matrix_tables: one table "Metrological characteristics" with columns and rows. Columns: indicating_device, nominal_diameter_dn, permanent_flow_rate_q3, overload_flow_rate_q4, q3_over_q1, q2_over_q1, position, length, connections, maximum_admissible_pressure, temperature_class, indicating_range, verification_scale_interval, accuracy_class, environmental_class, electromagnetic_influence_class, reverse_flow_measurement, power_supply, software_version. But the table layout: attributes as rows, values per DN as columns. The matrix_tables schema: columns[], rows[] object per row. I can pivot: columns = ["attribute", "DN50", "DN65", "DN80", "DN100"]. Rows per attribute. That preserves structure well.

column_units: [null, "mm", "m³/h", "m³/h", null, null, null, "mm", null, "bar", null, "m³", "10⁻⁵ m³", null, null, null, null, null, null].

That's reasonable.

Footnotes: marker "*", text "The water meter is not designed to measure reverse flow but can withstand an accidental reverse flow without any deterioration or change in metrological properties."

Page total: 2.

Now build JSON. Values numeric: Q4 31.250 → 31.25, 78.750 → 78.75.

type_level structured values — all values must be objects with value/unit_symbol/unit_id/footnote_markers. Let me follow rule 2 strictly: every characteristic value MUST be an object {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}.
